Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check As part of our commitment to safeguarding patients and staff, many roles at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) require a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. This is a standard process across the NHS and helps us ensure a safe environment for everyone. What is a DBS Check? A DBS check is a background check that reveals any criminal convictions, cautions, reprimands, or warnings. The level of check required depends on the role: Standard DBS : Checks for spent and unspent convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings. Enhanced DBS : Includes the above, plus any additional information held by local police thats considered relevant to the role. Enhanced with Barred Lists: Includes all of the above, plus checks against the childrens and/or adults barred lists. Who Needs a DBS Check Most roles involving direct patient contact, working with children or vulnerable adults, or access to sensitive information will require a DBS check. The job advert and recruitment team will let you know if this applies to your role. The Costs for a DBS At Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT), roles that require a DBS check are subject to a cost recovery policy. This means that the cost of submitting and processing a DBS application if you are successful and join us, will be deducted from your salary within the first three months of employment. If, however, you withdraw from a conditional offer after the DBS process has begun, you will still be liable for the cost incurred. description: We are looking for an enthusiastic, organised and motivated Booking Administrator to join our friendly and busy team at the Ely Community Diagnostic Centre, part of Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. Working as part of our administration team, you will be responsible for coordinating and booking patient appointments across a range of diagnostic services, including CT, MRI, Ultrasound, X-ray and other specialist investigations. You will also support the day-to-day running of the centre, responding to patient enquiries, managing referrals and providing reception cover when required. Community Diagnostic Centres are an exciting and expanding part of the NHS's long-term plans to transform diagnostic services, bringing essential tests and investigations closer to patient's homes, improving access to care and helping to reduce waiting times. As a relatively new and developing service, Ely CDC offers an opportunity to be part of this transformation, contributing to the growth and development of services that make a real difference to our local communities and the NHS. This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing service that is helping to bring essential NHS diagnostic investigations closer to patients' homes. The successful candidate will be responsible for providing an efficient, accurate and patient-focused administrative service, supporting the day-to-day delivery of diagnostic services at Ely Community Diagnostic Centre. Key responsibilities will include: Booking, rescheduling and cancelling patient appointments across a range of diagnostic services, ensuring appointments are managed in line with departmental procedures and waiting time targets.Managing incoming referrals and waiting lists, ensuring patients are booked appropriately and within required timescales.Monitoring appointment availability and working proactively to minimise unused capacity, helping the department make the best use of its diagnostic resources.Responding to patient enquiries by telephone and in person, providing clear and helpful information regarding appointments and investigations.Providing reception cover, including welcoming patients, checking them in for appointments and supporting the smooth running of clinics.Maintaining accurate and up-to-date patient records using electronic patient administration systems, including Epic.Liaising with clinical teams, colleagues and other departments to resolve booking queries and support effective patient pathways.Identifying and escalating booking issues, capacity concerns and potential delays to patient care.Supporting the achievement of departmental performance standards and NHS waiting time targets. Interviews are due to be held on 24th November 2026. All appointments with a start date on or after 1 October 2026 will be subject to a 12-week probationary period. This provides a structured and supportive period to help you settle into your role, with regular reviews and feedback. Just one of the ways we are working hard to support good working days at CUH. The successful candidate will be one of the first points of contact for patients contacting or visiting the practice. We are looking for someone with excellent communication and customer service skills who can provide a welcoming, professional and efficient service to our patients. This is a busy and varied role, requiring someone who can remain calm under pressure, use their initiative and work effectively as part of a team. Previous GP reception experience would be desirable but is not essential, as training will be provided. The hours for this vacancy are 22 hours per week, with the following working pattern: Monday: 12:30-18:30 Tuesday:12:00-17:00 Wednesday: 12:00-17:00 Thursday:12:30-18:30 Applicants should be able to commit to these hours. Booking, amending and cancelling appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Processing prescription requests and home visit requests in line with practice protocols. Passing messages and information accurately to the appropriate members of the clinical or administrative team. Dealing with patient queries and providing information about practice services and procedures. Maintaining accurate patient information and records using the practice's clinical computer system. Ensuring patient confidentiality is maintained at all times. Keeping the reception and waiting areas tidy and welcoming. Undertaking other reasonable reception and administrative duties as required. Use practice signposting and reception protocols to direct patients to the most appropriate service. Manage patients without appointments who require urgent advice in accordance with practice protocols, escalating concerns to a clinician or appropriate team when necessary. Process new patient registrations, check the reception email inbox daily and confirm patients reside within the practice catchment area. Explain practice arrangements and requirements to new and temporary patients, ensuring registration procedures are completed accurately. Take payments for private services and issue receipts in accordance with practice procedures, referring concerns to the secretarial team. Respond to patient and visitor enquiries professionally and promptly. Add home visit requests to the Urgent Care Team for review. Manage laboratory results received by telephone promptly and in accordance with practice protocols. Record patient signposting accurately using the appropriate EMIS Web template. Review incoming online consultation requests and process them in line with practice protocols, directing them to the appropriate clinician or service and escalating where necessary. Maintain familiarity with the appointment system, including routine and ad hoc changes. Book appointments in accordance with practice policy, seeking guidance from the Reception Supervisor when required. Ensure patient details on EMIS Web are accurate and up to date, including address, contact details and personal information. Ensure vaccines are recorded in the appropriate log, passed promptly to the nursing team and stored correctly. Forward invoices and delivery notes to the Deputy Practice Manager. Notify relevant staff of deliveries and ensure prescription paper deliveries are reported to the Prescriptions Team for logging and secure storage. To act as a chaperone during patient consultations or examinations when required, in accordance with the practice's Chaperone Policy. The post-holder must undertake any required training and follow the practice's procedures to ensure patient dignity, privacy and confidentiality are maintained. Inform the Deputy Practice Manager of damage, faulty equipment, complaints and other issues requiring attention. Undertake other reasonable duties in accordance with the needs of the practice. As the first point of contact for our patients, you will play a vital role in delivering a welcoming, professional and efficient service. Your responsibilities will include managing appointments, handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries, supporting patients with their needs, and carrying out a variety of administrative tasks, including processing clinical correspondence, Docman and eConsult workflows. Payments and Private Services Provide patients with information regarding fees for private and non-NHS services. Accept payments, issue receipts and maintain accurate records of transactions in accordance with Practice procedures. 6. Teamwork and General Responsibilities Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, administrative colleagues and the wider Practice team to ensure a high standard of patient service. Support colleagues during busy periods and contribute to the effective day-to-day running of the Practice. Follow all Practice policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and control, and confidentiality. title: Receptionist
description: Join our friendly, professional team as a Receptionist make a real impact in patient care. Were looking for a motivated and compassionate individual to join our warm and supportive GP practice team. As a key part of our front desk, you will be the first point of contact for patients, helping manage appointments, coordinate care, and keep the practice running smoothly. You will work in a team that values professionalism, kindness, and teamwork. Phlebotomy training will be provided, if you are interested. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy working with people, and want to be part of a practice that truly values its staff, we would love to hear from you. The contract would be for 20 hours per week to be worked over 3 days as follows: Mondays, Tuesdays 7.5 hours & Fridays 5 hours Shifts would alternate between 7:30-15:30 or 10:30-18:30, or 12-20:00 on a Monday, 11:30-19:30, or 7:30-15:30, or 10:30-18:30 on a Tuesday, and either 8-13:00 or 13:30-18:30 on a Friday. Main Duties of the Role Patient Reception & Enquiries: Greet patients and visitors in a welcoming and professional manner, manage general enquiries, and support patients through the appointment process. Appointment Management: Efficiently book and manage appointments using the practices clinical system, ensuring accurate patient details and smooth daily operations. Telephone Handling: Operate the phone system confidently, responding to patient needs, offering alternatives where needed (e.g., telephone consultations), and taking accurate messages. Administrative Support: Handle tasks such as scanning documents, processing referrals, photocopying, and ensuring records are updated with appropriate coding. Clinical Support: Assist with day-to-day practice needs, including preparation of consulting rooms and phlebotomy (training provided) . Repeat Prescriptions & Private Services: Process repeat prescription requests and inform patients of any charges for private services. New Patient Registrations: Register new patients in line with NHS guidelines and ensure theyre set up for an initial health check. Confidentiality & Teamwork: Maintain strict confidentiality and contribute positively to a collaborative, supportive team environment. Job Description RECEPTIONIST Accountable to: Practice Manager, Reception Manager JOB SUMMARY To deal with enquires from patients efficiently and courteously. To ensure health and safety procedures are maintained. KEY TASKS- 1. Receptions Duties Respond to all general enquiries and requests for assistance from patients and other visitors. Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking a temporary GP Greet and log in patients arriving for appointments directing and monitoring the flow of patients into consulting and treatments rooms. Ensure patients without appointments but who need urgent consultation are seen by a suitable clinician. Advise patients of relevant charges for private services: accept payment and issue receipts. To advise patients of our policy on repeat prescriptions, allowing 48 hours to complete, printing from patients computer medical records. Accepting messages and forwarding to the appropriate member of staff. Ensuring as much details have been taken: who is calling, what they are calling about, a contact number to ring them back on. Informing the relevant personnel when stock is running low Where necessary, clear information should be left for incoming colleagues regarding unresolved or urgent problems Ensure reception and waiting areas are kept clean and tidy 2. Management of Appointment System Endeavour to ensure the appointment system works as smoothly as possible Every effort should be made to ensure that the correct patient is booked, identifying name, address and date of birth. Any difficulties with system should be reported to relevant Support Desks 3. Requests for Visits As much detail as possible should be gained from a patient requesting a home visit: patients name, symptoms, brief history, and a contact telephone number to call them back. A summary printout will be printed. 4. Preparation of consulting rooms- Ensure all consulting rooms are tidy and prepared in readiness for each consulting session: including cleaning, ensuring there is enough couch roll, prescriptions and blank paper. Should the windows need opening for airing of the room, care should be taken to ensure that they are securely closed at the end of the day 5. Operation of Telephone System Receptionists must feel competent at using the telephone system and offering patients the choices if appointments are not available: such as a telephone consultation, or a message left for the duty doctor. Ensuring the telephone is picked up quickly and if a colleague is busy answering their telephone 6. Scanning and Read Coding All new correspondence will be scanned and workflowed electronically for action to the appropriate personnel. Any further action that the GP has requested must be taken. Any action taken from the document must be coded using the appropriate read codes electronically 7. Blood Samples Ensure that all samples are collected from the clinical team at specified times every day. Place in the plastic bag ready for collection by the courier 8. Photocopying You may be required to photocopy from time to time. Photocopying of patients medical records on behalf of solicitors or insurance companies must be dealt with promptly. The patients consent to release their medical records should be given before posting the copies to outside agencies. 9. Start and End of Day Procedures You are required to arrive at work 10 minutes before you are due to start, this gives you time to unlock doors and filing cabinets and to log in to the computer. You must be ready to work at your starting time. At the end of each day you must check all windows, doors and filing cabinets are locked. Any patient identifiable data is out of sight and that all lights are switched off. 10. Referrals and Letters Forward referrals/correspondence as directed by clinical staff to appropriate health professional. 11. Taking on New Patients All patients despite their visa status will be registered with the practice as long as they live within the practices catchment area (a copy of this area is available in reception) The patient can be asked for some form of ID to prove their name and address before registering a patient. Once ID has been shown they will complete a GMS1 form (purple form) and an appointment will be made with the Practice Nurse for a General Health Check. 12. Other requirements of the post To understand and adhere to strict confidentiality To maintain a positive attitude and manner towards patients and colleagues To work as part of a team and as such will share tasks including filing and making tea and coffee Compliance with practice policies and procedures including Health & Safety KEY RESPONSIBILITIES To participate in meetings as necessary Participate in your annual appraisal To maintain a professional development by attending external and in house training sessions arranged by the Practice Manager The duties above are subject to periodic review with the post holder

The role of Care Navigator is critical in the provision of services and ensuring that patients are able to access the most appropriate services for their needs, and will include a range of face to face, telephone and administrative work. This vacancy has arisen following the planned retirement of a member of the team at the end of December 2026, and we are looking to cover this post from 4th January 2027. Please read on and see our attached Practice Profile, job description and person specification for more details about us, the job, the hours and pay, and how to apply. NO AGENCIES - emails from employment agencies will be ignored. In the role of Care Navigator you would be working within the fantastic and dedicated Care Navigator team to provide responsive and professional reception and patient navigation services to our 13,500 or so patients. The team currently comprises 12 care navigators who all work a range of part time working patterns. The surgery is currently open to the public from 08.00-18.30 Monday to Friday. Our Care Navigation (Reception) services are normally based in reception on the ground floor and in the Care Navigator room or alongside the triage GP in the triage room on the first floor, and all Care Navigators spend time working in all areas, covering a range of face to face, telephone and administrative tasks. To be successful in this role, we would expect candidates to have experience of working within a busy reception, service or customer-focused environment, have excellent interpersonal skills, able to demonstrate a high standard of language and IT literacy, attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm under pressure. While primary care experience and knowledge of Emis Web may be an advantage, it is not essential as full training would be provided. The purpose of this post is to provide Care Navigator (Receptionist) services for the practice. General Duties Sign-post patients appropriately to practice services in accordance with the navigation Standard Operating Procedures. Assist with routine administrative tasks from other departments. Initiate contact with and respond to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers. To undertake specific assigned tasks, project support, or development / change work which may arise from time to time, under the direction of the relevant line manager. Participate in development plans for the practice and their implementation. Provide reception, sign-posting and administrative support for seasonal and/or exceptional public health campaigns such as, but not limited to, mass vaccination clinics. Reception Make appointments for patients attending or calling by telephone, using the computer system, and in accordance with the Practices appointment protocols. Assist patients where required with completion of e-consult forms. Contact patients to make arrangements for appointments and other actions in accordance with instructions of Triage GPs. Receive telephone requests for home visits. Receive general telephone enquiries and transfer callers to other surgery staff as appropriate. Receive requests for repeat prescriptions. Give out letters, reports, or forms to patients attending, and take payments where applicable in accordance with the navigation Standard Operating Procedures. Records & Triage As above Receive overflow of telephone calls and sign-post patients appropriately to practice services in accordance with the navigation Standard Operating Procedures. Process new patient registrations Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with the practice procedure. Processing of GPP workflow and tasks. Respond to requests for results and other clinical information in accordance with practice policy Liaise with GPs and other clinicians using the appropriate message system. Systems Administration & Support Retrieval and provision of information or documents from practice systems or external bodies as required. Assist with the cancellation and rebooking of doctor and other clinician appointment sessions as required and as directed by the Assistant Practice Manager or Care Navigator Service Manager. Liaise directly with hospital personnel, labs and other agencies with regard to medical matters. Liaise directly with patients by telephone or in person with regard to medical and administrative matters. Dignity at Work and Equality Statement We are committed to treating all of our staff and Service Users with dignity and respect. You are responsible for behaving in a way that is consistent with the aims of our Equality and Diversity Policy and the Equality Act (2010). This includes not discriminating unfairly in any area of your work and not bullying, harassing or otherwise intimidating other people. You should recognise and appreciate that people, both colleagues and service users are different and to act in ways that are consistent with their needs and preferences. You should at all times embody the ethos and values of Air Balloon Surgery and the Care Navigation Team, keeping patients at the heart of everything we do. Please see attached job description for more information.

title: Medical Administrator
description: We are looking for a reliable, enthusiastic and motivated individual who is committed to providing excellent patient care and is able to meet the requirements of a busy and growing Practice. We are a friendly family Practice, committed to delivering safe, high-quality services in innovative ways. As a large, well-established and forward-thinking GP Practice, we are proud to serve a registered patient population of approximately 42,000 patients. As our Practice continues to grow and develop, we are looking for someone to join our Medical Administrative Team who is flexible and adaptable to the needs of the service. This is a varied and rewarding front-line role, combining medical administration and reception responsibilities. You will play an important part in supporting our patients, clinicians and wider multidisciplinary team, helping to ensure the smooth and effective day-to-day running of the Practice. If you enjoy working in a busy environment, take pride in providing excellent customer service and are looking for a role where you can make a real difference to patients, we would love to hear from you. We welcome informal chats or visits, if you are interested, please contact Gillian Cawkill Head of HR & Governance gilliancawkill@nhs.net Unfortunately, we are unable to accept applications from individuals who require UK visa sponsorship. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK at the time of application. As a Medical Administrator, you will be one of the first points of contact for our patients and will provide a professional, helpful and compassionate service across a range of administrative and reception functions. Your duties will include, but are not limited to: Providing a friendly, professional and helpful first point of contact for patients, both face-to-face and by telephone. Handling telephone calls, digital contacts, practice emails and patient enquiries appropriately and efficiently. Undertaking medical administration and supporting the administrative elements of clinical triage. Maintaining patient confidentiality at all times. Contributing to the smooth and efficient running of the Practice. The role can be busy and fast-paced, and you will need to remain calm, professional and helpful when working under pressure. You will be expected to treat patients, visitors and colleagues with courtesy and respect and contribute to a welcoming and positive Practice environment. Working Hours 37.5 hours per week (full-time) preferred. We may also consider applications from candidates seeking a minimum of 30 hours per week. Working hours will be scheduled within the Practice's opening hours: Monday to Friday: 08:00-18:30 Saturday: 09:00-17:00 The role may include a regular requirement to work until 6.30 pm on Fridays. Candidates must therefore be able to work the required Friday late finish as part of their working pattern. We are looking for someone who is: Reliable, organised, and able to work effectively in a busy environment. Confident communicating with patients, colleagues and external organisations. Flexible and adaptable to the changing needs of a busy GP Practice. Able to manage competing priorities while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail. Professional, approachable and committed to delivering excellent patient service. Comfortable working across both administrative and reception functions. Able to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team. Confident using computer systems and willing to learn new systems and processes. Able to use their own initiative while also recognising when to seek advice or support. Committed to maintaining confidentiality and high standards of information governance. Able to demonstrate our values of Compassion, Respect, Learning, Quality and Integrity in their everyday work. Previous administrative experience and a strong background in customer service are essential. Previous experience of working within primary care, the NHS or another healthcare environment would be advantageous. However, we will provide training on Practice-specific systems and processes.

The role involves face-to-face, telephone and online patient enquiries, appointment administration and general administrative duties to support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. The ideal candidate will have excellent communication and customer service skills, a calm and professional manner, and the ability to work effectively in a busy environment while maintaining patient confidentiality and delivering a high standard of care. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and courteous manner. Check patients in for appointments and update their arrival status on the clinical system. Respond to patient enquiries in person, by telephone and through online communication channels. Assist patients with appointment bookings, cancellations and rearrangements in line with practice procedures. Treat all patients with dignity, respect, sensitivity and confidentiality. Communicate effectively with patients from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds. Manage difficult or distressed patients calmly and professionally, escalating concerns when necessary. Ensure patients who require additional assistance are supported appropriately. 2. Telephone and Appointment Management Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally. Handle appointment requests in accordance with practice policies and access procedures. Direct calls to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Take accurate messages and ensure they are passed to the relevant person in a timely manner. Explain practice procedures, appointment arrangements and available services clearly. Recognise when a call may require urgent clinical attention and follow the practice's approved escalation procedures. Never provide clinical advice beyond the receptionist's level of training and authorised responsibilities. Use the practice's clinical computer system, SystmOne, Use the practice's clinical computer system, such as EMIS Web or SystmOne, as applicable. Register patient arrivals and update demographic and contact details in accordance with practice procedures. Maintain accurate electronic records and administrative information. Process incoming and outgoing correspondence as directed. Scan, code or file documents in accordance with practice protocols and staff training. Support the processing of prescription requests, medical records requests and other administrative tasks within the scope of the role. Assist with recalls, patient registrations, appointment lists and other routine administrative work. Ensure all information is recorded accurately and handled securely. Maintain strict patient confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, NHS information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures relating to safeguarding children and adults at risk, escalating concerns promptly to the appropriate person. Maintain awareness of confidentiality when speaking on the telephone or at the reception desk. Verify patient identity and follow the practice's procedures before disclosing information. Report any data breaches, confidentiality concerns or incidents to the Practice Manager promptly. Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, managers and other administrative colleagues. Support the daily running of reception, ensuring the reception area remains organised and professional. Assist with incoming post, emails, document handling and general office duties. Follow practice policies, standard operating procedures and health and safety requirements. Attend staff meetings, training sessions and appraisals as required. Assist colleagues during periods of high demand and provide appropriate cover when required. Undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the role and level of responsibility.
